slot.brief: Show field-line patterns around a bar of material in a uniform field; identify which diagram represents a paramagnet/diamagnet/ferromagnet and give reasoning.

stem: Three bars are placed separately in the same uniform magnetic field directed from left to right, as shown in the figure. Which assignment of materials to bars is correct?

verdicts.working: A diverts field lines away from the bar (diamagnetic); B shows slight concentration (paramagnetic); C shows strong concentration (ferromagnetic).

working:
Field lines are expelled from a diamagnet: $B_{\text{inside}}<B_{\text{outside}}$ (A).
They are weakly concentrated in a paramagnet (B).
They are strongly concentrated in a ferromagnet (C).

Independent check: A diverts field lines away from the bar (diamagnetic); B shows slight concentration (paramagnetic); C shows strong concentration (ferromagnetic).

draft.stem: Three bars are placed separately in the same uniform magnetic field directed from left to right, as shown in the figure. Which assignment of materials to bars is correct?

figure.description: Draw three side-by-side panels labelled A, B and C, each containing an identical horizontal rectangular bar. In each panel, show a uniform magnetic field directed left to right: field lines are horizontal and equally spaced far from the bar, with arrowheads pointing right. In panel A, show the lines bending away from the bar so that they are less dense inside it than in the surrounding space. In panel B, show a modestly greater density of lines inside the bar than outside. In panel C, show a much greater density of lines through the bar, with lines bending inward toward it. Keep the bar outlines and panel sizes identical; do not include material names.

draft.working:
Field lines are expelled from a diamagnet: $B_{\text{inside}}<B_{\text{outside}}$ (A).
They are weakly concentrated in a paramagnet (B).
They are strongly concentrated in a ferromagnet (C).
draft.distractor_notes: B swaps the diamagnetic and paramagnetic patterns; C swaps the paramagnetic and ferromagnetic patterns; D reverses the diamagnetic and ferromagnetic assignments.
